---
title: "Benchmark: where write time goes"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = TRUE)
results <- function(name) {
  path <- file.path("..", "..", "bench", "results", paste0(name, ".parquet"))
  tibble::as_tibble(arrow::read_parquet(path))
}
write <- results("write")
counters <- results("write-counters")
knitr::read_chunk(file.path("..", "..", "bench", "write.R"))
has_ggplot <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
step_names <- c("geocode", "sort", "serialise", "hash", "check", "upload", "verify", "catalogs")
```

This article reads stored results; it does not run the benchmark. The script
is `bench/write.R`; its code is shown below as it was run.

## Question

`store_write()` geocodes geospatial rows, sorts and partitions them,
serialises them to Parquet in a staging folder, hashes the files, checks
sampled rows against `x`, uploads the files, verifies their MD5 in the
location and switches the catalogs. Where does the time go, does a second
set of geocoding workers (`options(rcs.workers = 4)`) help, and what does
writing to Google Cloud Storage cost compared with a local folder?

## Setup

```{r}
env <- write[1, grep("^env_", names(write))]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  item = sub("^env_", "", names(env)),
  value = vapply(env, function(v) as.character(v[[1]]), character(1)),
  row.names = NULL
))
```

Simulated data only: `rcs_sim_table()` written with its key and
`partition = "year"`, and `rcs_sim_polygons()` written with
`partition = "h3"`, each at 1e5 and 1e6 rows. Every repetition writes into a
new, empty store, so every write is a first write. The cloud store lies under
a random prefix of a test bucket, removed at the end; only 1e5 rows are
written there, to keep the uploads small. Each case is timed with
`bench_run()` (five repetitions, median reported).

The steps are timed by wrapping the package's internal step functions for
the duration of the script: `geo_encode()` (geocode, which also puts the
geospatial rows in written order), `sort_rows()` and `partition_plan()`
(sort, including the choice of the H3 partition resolution),
`files_write_parquet()` (serialise), `md5_file()` (hash), `check_staged()`
(check), `be_put()` (upload), `be_md5()` (verify) and the catalog reads and
writes. A step called inside another one counts only for itself. What is
left of the total ("other") is argument checks, entries, manifests and
staging-folder housekeeping. The step medians are taken step by step, so
they need not add up exactly to the median total.

## Results

```{r}
shown <- write[c("case", "n", "median_s", "min_s", "max_s", "rows_per_s", "bytes_written")]
shown$median_s <- signif(shown$median_s, 3)
shown$min_s <- signif(shown$min_s, 3)
shown$max_s <- signif(shown$max_s, 3)
shown$rows_per_s <- round(shown$rows_per_s)
knitr::kable(shown, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

`bytes_written` is the total of the `bytes_up` counter of one write (data
files, index table, manifests and catalogs) for the cases with one worker.

```{r}
steps <- write[c("case", paste0("step_", step_names, "_s"))]
names(steps) <- c("case", step_names)
steps$other <- pmax(write$median_s - rowSums(steps[step_names]), 0)
long <- data.frame(
  case = rep(steps$case, times = length(step_names) + 1),
  step = factor(rep(c(step_names, "other"), each = nrow(steps)), levels = c(step_names, "other")),
  seconds = unlist(steps[c(step_names, "other")], use.names = FALSE)
)
share <- steps
share[c(step_names, "other")] <- round(100 * steps[c(step_names, "other")] / write$median_s)
knitr::kable(share, caption = "Share of the median write time per step, in percent.")
```

```{r, eval = has_ggplot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Horizontal stacked bars, one per benchmark case, showing the seconds of each step of a write: geocode, sort, serialise, hash, check, upload, verify, catalogs and other. Polygon writes are dominated by geocoding; table writes by the check and serialisation; writes to the cloud bucket add a long upload segment."}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(long, aes(x = seconds, y = case, fill = step)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Median seconds", y = NULL, fill = "Step") +
  theme_minimal()
```

One against four geocoding workers, polygons:

```{r}
poly <- write[write$kind == "polygons" & write$location == "local", ]
workers <- data.frame(
  rows = unique(poly$rows),
  total_1 = sapply(unique(poly$rows), function(r) poly$median_s[poly$rows == r & poly$workers == 1]),
  total_4 = sapply(unique(poly$rows), function(r) poly$median_s[poly$rows == r & poly$workers == 4]),
  geocode_1 = sapply(unique(poly$rows), function(r) poly$step_geocode_s[poly$rows == r & poly$workers == 1]),
  geocode_4 = sapply(unique(poly$rows), function(r) poly$step_geocode_s[poly$rows == r & poly$workers == 4])
)
workers[-1] <- signif(workers[-1], 3)
knitr::kable(workers, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Local folder against the cloud bucket, 1e5 rows, one worker:

```{r}
cloud <- write[write$rows == 1e5 & write$workers == 1, c("kind", "location", "median_s", "step_upload_s", "step_verify_s", "step_catalogs_s", "bytes_written")]
cloud$upload_mb_per_s <- round(cloud$bytes_written / 1e6 / cloud$step_upload_s, 1)
cloud[3:6] <- lapply(cloud[3:6], signif, 3)
knitr::kable(cloud[order(cloud$kind, cloud$location), ], format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Backend calls of one write (work counters, deterministic):

```{r}
calls <- counters[counters$counter == "backend_call", ]
calls <- stats::aggregate(n ~ case + location + detail, data = calls, FUN = sum)
wide <- stats::reshape(calls, idvar = c("case", "location"), timevar = "detail", direction = "wide")
names(wide) <- sub("^n\\.", "", names(wide))
wide[is.na(wide)] <- 0
knitr::kable(wide[order(wide$case, wide$location), ], row.names = FALSE)
```

## Verdict

```{r, include = FALSE}
pick <- function(kind, rows, location = "local", workers = 1) {
  write[write$kind == kind & write$rows == rows & write$location == location & write$workers == workers, ]
}
big <- max(write$rows)
p1 <- pick("polygons", big)
p4 <- pick("polygons", big, workers = 4)
t1 <- pick("table", big)
pct <- function(row, step) round(100 * row[[paste0("step_", step, "_s")]] / row$median_s)
pg <- pick("polygons", 1e5, "gcs")
pl <- pick("polygons", 1e5)
tg <- pick("table", 1e5, "gcs")
tl <- pick("table", 1e5)
```

- Polygons: geocoding is the largest step,
  `r pct(p1, "geocode")`% of a write of
  `r format(big, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)` polygons with one
  worker (`r round(p1$rows_per_s)` rows per second in all). The H3
  partition choice (in "sort") takes `r pct(p1, "sort")`%; serialising
  `r pct(p1, "serialise")`%. The partition choice asks for the H3 parent of
  every row at each resolution it tries, although the rows hold only a few
  distinct cells (883 at 1e5 rows); taking the parents of the distinct cells and
  matching them back gave the same result about 18 times faster on 1e5
  polygons.
- Tables: the serialization check takes `r pct(t1, "check")`% of a write of
  `r format(big, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)` rows, more than
  serialising them (`r pct(t1, "serialise")`%); throughput
  `r format(round(t1$rows_per_s), big.mark = ",")` rows per second. The
  check compares 20 rows per file but restores the R types of the whole row
  group it reads (50,000 rows, the list column element by element in R)
  before taking them: about 0.5 s per file, against a few milliseconds when
  the 20 rows are taken first.
- Four workers against one: `r signif(p1$median_s, 3)` s against
  `r signif(p4$median_s, 3)` s for `r format(big, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)`
  polygons (geocode `r signif(p1$step_geocode_s, 3)` s against
  `r signif(p4$step_geocode_s, 3)` s). At 1e5 rows four workers cannot help:
  the rows form one chunk of `rcs.chunk_size` (1e5), and only chunks are
  shared out; the difference at 1e5 rows is noise of the busy machine. At
  `r format(big, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)` rows the geocoding
  gains a factor of `r signif(p1$step_geocode_s / p4$step_geocode_s, 2)`
  with four workers, not four. Part of `geo_encode()` stays in the main
  process (WKB conversion, sorting, the index table) and the chunks are
  copied to the workers; how the remainder splits was not measured.
- The cloud bucket adds the upload: `r signif(pg$median_s, 3)` s against
  `r signif(pl$median_s, 3)` s for 1e5 polygons, `r signif(tg$median_s, 3)` s
  against `r signif(tl$median_s, 3)` s for 1e5 table rows. MD5 verification
  reads object metadata and costs `r signif(pg$step_verify_s, 2)` s per
  write, small next to the upload.

## Limits

- One machine; two other agents ran tests and rendered documents on it
  while this benchmark ran, so absolute times carry noise (compare `min_s`
  with `median_s`). The baseline is measured again on a quiet machine.
- The cloud upload speed is that of this machine's network connection; it
  bounds every cloud number here.
- The step times come from wrapping internal functions; the wrappers add a
  few microseconds per call, and the H3 partition choice is reported inside
  "sort".
- `bench_run()` measures memory (`mem_alloc_bytes`, R allocations only) in a
  separate evaluation of the first repetition; peak memory is measured in
  `benchmark-scale.Rmd`.
- Writes with history, updates and replaces of existing datasets, and
  secondaries are not measured here.
